ja: 気になっているのは、クライアントがまだ私たちの提案に返事をくれていないことです。
en: What worries me is that the client hasn't replied to our proposal yet.
alternatives: What concerns me is that the client still hasn't responded to our proposal.
What I'm worried about is that the client hasn't gotten back to us on our proposal yet.
point: 「気になっているのは」は What worries me is that で始める

ja: 先方から見積書が届いたら、私がすぐにチームに共有しますね。
en: As soon as the client sends the estimate, I'll share it with the team.
alternatives: I'll share the estimate with the team as soon as the client sends it.
When the client sends the estimate, I'll share it with the team right away.
point: as soon as の後は未来のことでも現在形 sends にする

ja: 倉庫でトラブルがあったため、残りの部品の納品は来週まで延期されました。
en: Due to a problem at the warehouse, delivery of the remaining parts has been postponed until next week.
alternatives: Because of a problem at the warehouse, the remaining parts won't be delivered until next week.
Delivery of the rest of the parts has been delayed until next week because of a warehouse problem.
point: 納品が主語なので has been postponed と受け身にする

ja: 課長、この件はいつまでに終わらせればいいですか？
en: When do I need to have this done by?
alternatives: When should I get this done by?
What's the deadline for this?
point: 「いつまでに」は文末に by を残して期限を聞く

ja: テストはまだ全部終わっていませんが、私たちは金曜のリリースには間に合う見込みです。
en: Although we haven't finished all the tests yet, we expect to make the Friday release.
alternatives: We haven't finished all the testing yet, but we should still make the Friday release.
Even though testing isn't finished yet, we expect to be ready for Friday's release.
point: although の後に but は重ねない

ja: 昨夜3時にサーバーが止まって、約200人のユーザーがログインできなくなりました。
en: The server went down at 3 a.m. last night, leaving about 200 users unable to log in.
alternatives: The server crashed at 3 a.m. last night, and about 200 users couldn't log in.
At 3 a.m. last night the server went down, which left about 200 users unable to log in.
point: 結果は , leaving 〜 unable to の分詞でつなげる

ja: うちのチームにあと一人エンジニアがいれば、今週中にテストを終えられるんですが。
en: If we had one more engineer on the team, we'd be able to finish the testing by the end of this week.
alternatives: If our team had one more engineer, we could finish the testing by the end of this week.
If we had another engineer on the team, we'd be able to get the testing done by the end of the week.
point: 現実と違う仮定なので had と we'd／could を使う

ja: 営業チームは、締め切りを来週まで延ばすことを検討しています。
en: The sales team is thinking about extending the deadline to next week.
alternatives: The sales team is considering extending the deadline to next week.
The sales team is thinking of pushing the deadline back to next week.
point: about や consider の後ろは to 不定詞ではなく -ing 形

ja: リリース前にこのバグのことを知っていればよかったんですが、気づいたのは今朝でした。
en: I wish I'd known about this bug before the release, but I only noticed it this morning.
alternatives: I wish I had found out about this bug before the release, but I didn't notice it until this morning.
I wish I'd known about this bug before the release, but I didn't catch it until this morning.
point: 過去の後悔は wish の後を had + 過去分詞にする

ja: 部長、企画書はもう完成しています。
en: The proposal is ready now.
alternatives: The proposal is finished now.
The proposal is done now.
point: 「完成している」は be 動詞＋ready で言える

ja: そのデータの不一致、午前中からずっと調べてるんですか？よければ私が手伝いますよ。
en: Have you been looking into that data mismatch all morning? I can help if you'd like.
alternatives: Have you been working on that data discrepancy since this morning? I'm happy to help if you want.
Have you been trying to sort out that data mismatch all morning? I can give you a hand if you like.
point: 「ずっと〜している」は Have you been -ing で表す

ja: 先週はデザインでかなり苦労しましたが、今はもう大きな問題はすべて解決しました。
en: We struggled a lot with the design last week, but we've now solved all the major issues.
alternatives: We had a hard time with the design last week, but we've already fixed all the big problems.
The design gave us a lot of trouble last week, but we've now resolved all the major issues.
point: last week は過去形、今の完了は現在完了で分ける

ja: この件、もう部長に相談しましたか？まだなら、午後に一緒に行きましょう。
en: Have you talked to the manager about this yet? If not, let's go together this afternoon.
alternatives: Have you already discussed this with the manager? If you haven't, let's go see them together this afternoon.
Have you asked the manager about this yet? If not, let's talk to them together this afternoon.
point: 「もう〜した？」は現在完了の疑問文、文末に yet

ja: 先方からまだ返信がないので、私が間違ったアドレスに送ってしまったのかもしれません。
en: The client still hasn't replied, so I might have sent it to the wrong address.
alternatives: I may have sent it to the wrong address, since the client hasn't replied yet.
Since we haven't heard back from the client, I might have used the wrong address.
point: 過去の推量は might have + 過去分詞

ja: 私がもっと早くご相談していれば、この遅れは防げたと思います。
en: If I'd come to you sooner, I think we could have avoided this delay.
alternatives: If I had talked to you earlier, I think we could have prevented this delay.
I think this delay could have been avoided if I'd consulted you sooner.
point: 過去の仮定は If I had 〜, could have 過去分詞

ja: 今、田中さんと一緒に来週のプレゼンの資料を作っているところです。
en: I'm working on next week's presentation with Tanaka-san now.
alternatives: I'm making the slides for next week's presentation with Tanaka-san now.
Tanaka-san and I are preparing next week's presentation now.
point: 「〜しているところ」は現在進行形 I'm ~ing

ja: 部長、新しいやり方のほうが前のやり方よりずっと速いです。
en: The new process is much faster than the old one.
alternatives: The new method is a lot faster than the old one.
The new way is much quicker than the old one.
point: 比較級を強めるのは very ではなく much や a lot

ja: 部長、新しい勤怠システムがいつ使えるようになるか、ご存じですか？
en: Do you know when the new attendance system will be ready?
alternatives: Do you know when we can start using the new attendance system?
Do you have any idea when the new attendance system will be ready?
point: when の後ろは will the system ではなく主語＋動詞の順

ja: テストの結果がおかしかったので、今、新人に全部のログを一から確認し直してもらっています。
en: The test results looked off, so I'm having our new hire go through all the logs again from scratch.
alternatives: The test results seemed strange, so I'm having our new team member check all the logs again from the beginning.
Since the test results looked wrong, I'm getting our new hire to recheck all the logs from scratch.
point: have＋人＋動詞の原形。to を付けない（get なら to が要る）

ja: 課長、この不具合について、少しアドバイスをいただけますか？
en: Could you give me some advice about this bug?
alternatives: Could you give me some advice on this bug?
Could I ask for some advice about this bug?
point: advice は数えられないので an advice や advices にしない

ja: すみません、今の人数だと、うちのチームでは今月中に全部の注文をさばけません。
en: Sorry, our team can't handle all the orders this month with the current staff.
alternatives: Sorry, with the current staff, our team can't process all the orders this month.
Sorry, our team can't get all the orders done this month with the current staff.
point: 「注文をさばく」は handle the orders

ja: バグの原因はまだ調べているところですが、近いうちに私からまたご連絡します。
en: I'm still looking into the cause of the bug, but I'll get back to you soon.
alternatives: I'm still trying to figure out what's causing the bug, but I'll get back to you shortly.
I'm still investigating the cause of the bug, but I'll let you know soon.
point: 「調べる」は look into、「また連絡する」は get back to you

ja: 先週おっしゃっていた新しいツールをいつから使い始めるのか、もう決められましたか？
en: Have you decided yet when we'll start using the new tool you mentioned last week?
alternatives: Have you decided when we're going to start using the new tool you talked about last week?
Have you made a decision yet on when we'll start using the new tool you mentioned last week?
point: when 以下は疑問文の語順にせず we'll start の順
